correctness.rationale: Zaidi–Jamil defines the n-dimensional × test hypercube J_n^× as the complete graph on {0,1}^n. Its hypergraph morphisms are precisely maps whose images are cliques in the two-section graph when all vertices lie in hyperedges. After dividing coordinate-degenerate maps, the chain complex is normalized all-coordinate Boolean maps with image in a flag simplex. A fixed vertex order sends [v0,...,vn] to the corner cube selecting v_max active index, else v0; direct face calculation shows it is a signed chain map. On any full simplex, the last-coordinate cone to a chosen simplex vertex contracts normalized chains integrally. Exact basiswise Mayer–Vietoris short exact sequences for unions of simplicial subcomplexes and induction with five lemma establish a quasi-isomorphism on every finite flag complex and integral torsion, not just mod-two Betti numbers. Independent exact corner-boundary identities verified dimensions 1..6. The proof does not confuse this complete test graph with ordinary Hamming cube adjacency.
residual_risks: Contraction must choose w inside the particular full simplex; original finite checker chooses a global w when testing arbitrary subcomplexes, so its cone test alone is not an all-simplex proof
The map is strictly natural for common ordered inclusions, not arbitrary vertex maps
